course_name_original: Elasticidad Y Resistencia De Materiales I
course_name_en: Elasticity and Strength of Materials I
prerequisites: Prior knowledge from basic subjects, particularly Mechanics (first year, second semester).

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and use of the principles of strength of materials.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies typically demonstrated by formulating and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.
Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.

syllabus_topics: Stress state in the points of an elastic solid
Strain state in the vicinity of a point
Relations between stress and strain states
Introduction to the study of Strength of Materials
Deformation of beams subjected to bending
teaching_methods: Learning (reading and comprehension) of basic bibliography text
Tutorial action (in-person, when possible, and virtual)
Self-assessment activities (solving self-check exercises, completing continuous assessment tests)
assessment_rules: The final grade (NF) is calculated as NF = 0.95*NE + 0.05*NP if no PECs are evaluated, or NF = 0.15*NPECs + 0.80*NE + 0.05*NP if PECs are evaluated. NE is the exam grade, NPECs is the PEC grade, and NP is the lab practices grade. Laboratory practices are mandatory to pass the course, and their grade is considered if the sum of the approved exam and PEC grades is at least 4.5. A minimum exam grade of 4 is required to add the PEC grade. Both lab practices and in-person exam grades are retained for subsequent academic years, and PECs are considered in the extraordinary exam session.
